notes.title: Craft Your Own Story: Mystery Editor & Workshop content now available
notes.notes:
We are thrilled to let you know that two brand-new features for Whispers in the West—the Mystery Editor and Steam Workshop support are now live! 


[h2]The Mystery Editor
[/h2]
Have you ever wanted to create your own murder mystery? Now you can:

[list]
[*] Craft Your Own Story – Develop a one-day mini-mystery or an intricate three-day case.
[*] Test Your Script Instantly – Try out your custom script in-game via Steam and refine it as needed.
[*] Playtest with Friends – Gather your friends to playtest your mystery (and remember, friends always play for free!).
[*] Share with the Community – Once you're satisfied, upload your case to the Steam Workshop and share your creation with the wider community.
[/list]

[h2]Accessing the Editor
[/h2]
The Whispers in the West Mystery Editor is accessed online through your web browser. Go to https://editor.whispersinthewest.infinite-y.com/ and get started. (You will need to own a copy of the game first, of course).

[h2]First Workshop Case
[/h2]
In case you missed our previous announcement. A whole new case, Two Bad Sisters, will be free for all as the first workshop case.

Written by Jon Ingold, the acclaimed writer behind Overboard! and A Highland Song, Two Bad Sisters is a curious mystery that will challenge even the sharpest detectives.

The elegant Miss Sara Estelle has arrived in Brimstone, seeking your help to recover a valuable possession left with the priest. But there’s a twist—the priest insists she has already retrieved it! Who’s lying? Who’s telling the truth? And who’s simply mistaken? It’s up to you to uncover the mystery.

notes.title: [Dev Diary] Why do we offer cases as DLCs?
notes.notes:
A most-asked question about Whispers in the West is why we decided to offer the cases as DLCs instead of offering a one-off-purchase game. We totally get that this pricing is unconventional for Steam, and we truly accept all the criticism. 

Whispers in the West is more of an experiment than a commercial project. We are humbled by players’ preference to purchase all the cases at once - we truly didn’t expect this. 

So, we feel it's important to communicate our thought process, and we hope to deliver more value to our players in the future.

[h1]The team behind this little game
[/h1]
How the team behind Whispers in the West was formed is a story in itself.

In 2021, in an already competitive job market, the hiring freeze, as a result of the pandemic, made it challenging for graduates to get started in the games industry that year. So we formed Team Dissonant - almost all the team were recent graduates - and we wanted to make our own game.

Here came another challenge, we all work remotely and we had never met in person. Fortunately, we had games - we played many online multiplayer games together, as well as traditional murder mystery games over Discord. We loved murder mysteries and were surprised to find out there were very few options to play this type of games online, in particular, without the need for a game master (GM).

So we decided to take on this challenge - creating an online multiplayer murder mystery game that can be shared among friends and can be played without a GM.

This is not a typical "first quest" for a group of graduates - mostly for the challenges that come with multiplayer games, even experienced teams don't easily go down this path; not to mention the fact that there were so few multiplayer narrative games. 

The team did such an amazing job in making Whispers in the West a reality. And we are so grateful for the help we received along the way, namely, UK Games Fund and Wings.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41825657/0adfcb6faec9728bb7ee057752fe6aba1ebf19fa.jpg[/img]
[h1]The pricing of Whispers in the West
[/h1]
The core game of Whispers in the West is priced at $4.99, which includes all the content of the free demo plus an hour-long case, The Break-in. All the subsequent cases are offered as DLCs, each priced at $6.99 - however, you can get all the DLCs in a bundle at a massively discounted price, about $25 depending on where you are, which offers 6 - 8 hours of gameplay - and your friends can join the game completely for free - a much-loved feature. If you play a case with three more friends, after the bundle discount, the cost to each player is ($6.99 - 38% bundle discount) / 4 = $1.

We firmly believe games are better when shared with friends, that's why we make sure "Friends always play for free" in Whispers in the West. Whether it's the core game or the DLCs, as long as a case is owned by one of the players, other players can always join the room for free (using the demo). So, if there are two or more friends you like to play games with, the cost of each case for each person is no more than a cup of coffee.

A lesser-known Steam tip is that, the type of bundle of Whispers in the West is called "Complete The Set" - meaning that even if you own part of the content in the bundle, you will only pay for the content you haven't owned when you purchase the bundle. So, for example, if you have bought the core game and a DLC, and now you want to buy the full bundle, you will only be charged for the difference. You will never end up repaying for what you already bought.

Each case in Whispers in the West is an hour long - some players like this, some don't. We can probably talk about the inception of this game in more detail another day. In short, we purposely made the game short and digestible for players. Honestly, it would be much easier to write long dialogues (although there are already 17k words in each case on average because of the non-linear nature of the story). But we cannot expect friends who come to play a game together to spend hours and hours reading the lines. We want to offer quality time for players, by focusing on the deduction and debate.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41825657/d6b7e4f5a40560ab07379e16c6ad5dc76d84dc5c.jpg[/img]
[h1]So, why DLCs?
[/h1]
It's important to mention that, however uncommon it seems for Steam, it's quite a standard practice to offer murder mystery games on an episodic basis. Indeed, the average pricing for traditional murder mystery games is around $20 per case (if delivered electronically, physical copies are more expensive). And the typical length for a case is 2 - 3 hours.

One of the reasons is that, unlike for single-player games, players need to find time to organise game sessions for multiplayer games. This can be challenging for some of us who are only able to play games like this once or twice a year. So, we did not price the game in an attempt to hook or scam the players - quite the opposite - we don't want to force players to pay for the content they don't need.

Another idea we have for Whispers in the West is that, if the game turns out to be successful, we want to invite guest writers to create cases for the game. Offering each case as a separate DLC gives us the flexibility to do this kind of collaboration.



We genuinely welcome different opinions and we do understand why some players feel uncomfortable about the pricing. We will do our best to deliver more value to our players in the future. In fact, we are working on a custom case editor, so anyone can write their own mysteries, play with friends, upload the cases to Steam workshop and share with the wider community - this will be offered completely for free.
 
Last but not least, making independent games in today’s economic climate is not easy. Every comment you leave on Steam can potentially have an impact on the members of the team. Similarly, if you recognise our values, please do not hesitate to offer us some words of encouragement. Thank you.

notes.title: Hot fix: We fixed an issue in the Giraffe case
notes.notes:
Hey, detectives!

We have some important news about the Giraffe case. **A sneaky bug was tripping you up on Day 2, and we're truly sorry for the disruption!** We owe a huge thanks to the eagle-eyed players who helped us track it down.


This one's entirely on us – a silly mistake on our part. But the good news is, **we've just pushed a hotfix to fix the issue** If you had to leave the case unsolved before, now's your chance to dust off your magnifying glass and give it another go. We promise, the story's definitely worth the second look. 


**P.S.** This fix should work for most of you, but if you're playing **offline**, you might need to hold tight for a bit. We're working on a new build just for you, and it'll be with you as soon as possible.


We know how frustrating bugs can be, and we take testing seriously. We meticulously comb through every build before it hits Steam, but sometimes these little critters sneak past us. Rest assured, we're constantly learning and improving our processes to make sure your detective adventures are as smooth as possible.


Thanks for your patience and understanding. And as always, if you encounter issues that impact your game experience, please do let us know in the Community Hub. This will help us a million!

notes.title: How to set up Twitch integration
notes.notes:
[previewyoutube=VJFoGRbynoU;full][/previewyoutube]

The Twitch integration enables your audience to interact with you in the game through the Twitch chat.

[list]
[*]Your viewers can prompt you to ask about something or someone by typing in the chat command "!ask [a character or a letter]"
[*]Your viewers can vote on the answers by using the chat command "!vote [a character or a letter]"
[/list]


[h1]Get the OAuth code for your Twitch account
[/h1]
[olist]
[*]Go to [url=https://twitchapps.com/tmi/]https://twitchapps.com/tmi/[/url] in the browser where you are logged in with your Twitch account. 
[*]Click "Connect".
[*]On the next page, "Authorize" the Twitch Chat OAuth Token Generator app to read your channel's chat messages.
[*]Then, you should see an OAuth token starting with "oauth".
[*]Copy this token (including "oauth:").
[/olist]

* To remove the permission, go to Twitch settings.

[h1]Enter the OAuth code in Whispers in the West
[/h1]
[olist]
[*]Launch Whispers in the West from Steam
[*]On the case selection screen, click the gear icon on the top right.
[*]Then go to "Steaming"
[*]Enter the name of your Twitch channel, and the OAuth token you copied in the previous step.
[*]Optionally, you can save your token in the game.
[*]Slide the "Connect to Twitch" toggle to the right
[*]Once you see "Connected", start a game and your audience will be able to interact with you 
[/olist]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41825657/50fdf0d1a6b94bcaee5e759ac93b6aa07d39aa58.png[/img]

notes.title: Launch Week Discount
notes.notes:
For the launch week only, you can buy the all-six-case bundle at a 50% discount.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41825657/0d818bbfa3fd472c6ccefb69bffd75b762a2388d.png[/img]
[b]The Break-in[/b]: The Break-in comes with the base game. Dawn breaks to find the Brimstone Bank broken open. What comes spilling out could bury this town. It's time to roll up your sleeves and get sleuthing, before everything unravels.

[b]The Cult[/b]: A grizzly murder with an old-fashioned weapon! A town overrun with superstition and paranoia! An inventor and “saviour” who claims he can remake the world! Four investigators to make sense of it all before it's too late.

[b]The Ghost[/b]: The Brimstone mine has swallowed a victim! Old resentments are rising from the dead. Only the truth can banish what is to come. Brimstone needs a team who aren't afraid of no ghost to bust this case.

[b]The Giraffe[/b]: The circus is in town and passions are as high as a giraffe's head. Can the famously murder-happy residents of Brimstone enjoy the exotic delights of the circus without butchering one another in the dark?

[b]The Cocktail[/b]: The who's who of Brimstone is throwing a party after an incredible windfall. The ice is cold, the drinks are exotic, and the odds of survival are... about the same.

[b]The Curse[/b]: Something has been festering in the heart of Brimstone for years. Escalating events reveal a disturbing truth at the core of Brimstone. Will you be able to solve the mystery and bring the secrets to light?

Each case is designed to be solved in about 60 - 90 minutes - that’s 6 - 9 hours of gameplay guaranteed in the initial release. Although, if you are playing solo, it’s likely to take a little longer. 

[h2]Friends play for free
[/h2]
As promised, Whispers in the West is a point-and-click adventure with a twist - as a player, you can either go solo or collaborate with family or friends. 
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41825657/839f5b48ce32cdad45d1d81847f2b2436a6f10de.jpg[/img]
Unlike many co-op games, Whispers in the West doesn’t require those who are invited to buy another copy of the game. Anyone can join a room using the Steam demo for free, as long as the host owns the game. Because we are a firm believer that games are better with friends, and friends should play for free.

Can’t find people to play with? Head to the [url=https://discord.gg/BFU4Khvfnw]gamer-pals channel[/url] on our Discord server and make new friends.

[h2]Twitch Integration for Streamers
[/h2]
Whispers in the West could not have existed without our previous Twitch streamers and their community. To support streamers better engaging with their audience, we designed a Twitch integration that enables viewers to interact with the streamer in the game through chat - viewers can prompt the streamers to check on a suspect or vote on the final answers. 
[previewyoutube=VJFoGRbynoU;full][/previewyoutube]

[h2]Multi-languages for the Base Game
[/h2]
For gamers from 🇲🇽 🇦🇷 🇪🇸 🇩🇪 🇨🇱 🇨🇴 🇯🇵 🇺🇾 🇻🇪 and beyond, we are glad to announce that the base game will be available in English, Spanish, German and Japanese. However, the DLCs are in English only at the moment.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41825657/e7381978b78a1e2ddc323f0460f5f8b23b8b68e7.png[/img]
Sorry, we’d really like to offer the full game to a global audience, but unfortunately, our budget doesn’t allow us to localise the full game or in more languages. That’s why, if you’d like to see more content in your language, please let the world know - that’s the only way we can do it.

[h2]Here are some ways you can help us
[/h2]
👯‍♀️ Enjoy the game with friends 
🐦 [url=https://twitter.com/TeamDissonant]Tweet or retweet about us [/url]
📺 Let your favourite streamers or YouTubers know about Whispers in the West - [url=https://www.lurkit.com/campaigns/whispers-in-the-west]we are on Lurkit [/url]
💬 Join our Discord server discord.gg/CRfhJXvGRS

Most importantly, ✍️ Give us a review on Steam -

notes.title: 6 Essential Social Narrative Experiences
notes.notes:
Games are better with friends. Narrative or story-driven games are traditionally a single-player experience. However, with the rise of social narrative games, you don’t have to be a lone wolf any more. Social narrative games are all about experiencing a story with your friends along for the ride, often making choices about how things will play out.

We wanted to share some that have been getting us excited - 

-TickTock A Tale for Two

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41825657/05bf464fcfa786e04694251f987ae3ffe56bd039.jpg[/img]

We’ve found that playing a puzzle game with other people in the room is an inevitable recipe for frantic gesturing at the television screen, amiable bickering, and an altogether excellent time. TickTock: A Tale For Two does a great job of accentuating this experience by providing each player with differing information and requiring their communication to succeed. It’s interested in being cosy and involved in a way that similar more party-oriented games like Keep Talking And Nobody Explodes fundamentally aren’t. It’s well worth a look.

-King of the Castle

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41825657/cef37caad4165f8b929d351f4ed52918e95c97ea.jpg[/img]

King of the Castle really plays to the strengths of its medium. By casting you and your friends as monarchs and nobles, before setting you loose scheming against each other, it invites players to bring themselves into the game and build stories and jokes on its excellent foundations. It can be as crunchy as the legacy boardgame meetup you’re still struggling to schedule or as breezy as your lockdown Jackbox sessions. Best of all, it’s full of surprises.

-As Dusk Falls

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41825657/d4ebad63c34f029861952468192a1d2f4a2dc78b.jpg[/img]

As Dusk Falls is an award-winning entry in the genre of “films you’re supposed to talk over”. There are tons of opportunities to argue with your friends over precisely what to do, and with a maximum of 8 people playing at once, you can get pretty raucous with it. These multiplayer cinematic adventure games feel like they’re developing in an exciting direction, and we can’t wait to see more.

-Whispers In The West

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41825657/f642ca26dc67551f7d23638be16b3c1e9149e05f.jpg[/img]

Whispers In The West is our own multiplayer murder mystery game. In it, teams of up to four players investigate crimes in the Old West in real time. It’s all about splitting up whilst constantly communicating and comparing information. Where was the mayor at 10 am? Why does the butcher stammer when you ask her about her seasoning? What’s that spooky sound in the mine? And did everyone hear it? Whispers In The West is a party game that invites players to immerse themselves in the goings-on of the small town of Brimstone one 20-minute mystery at a time, in an ongoing story that plays out like a classic murder mystery television show.


-Chronicles Of Crime

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41825657/d2cc5cbb08cc7f059153048628b4530dcd9dd5b1.jpg[/img]

If a traditional face-to-face social experience is more of your thing, Chronicles Of Crime is a board game with maximalism that’s always worth a second look. It’s a board game with an app that supports virtual reality to boot. The mysteries you’re solving often link into bigger stories, and there’s something for everyone to talk about and loads of toys to play with.


-MUD

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41825657/44ca0ca7ad820df4c9c536bf371171b49e09808e.png[/img]

If you are feeling nostalgic, MUD or multi-user dungeon, was an avant-garde video game experience rooted back in the 1970s. It’s difficult to talk about multiplayer social experiences without someone eventually going dewy-eyed and recollecting the most exciting thing you’ve ever heard about their experience in MUD or one of its offshoots. MUD is directly responsible for some of the most astounding MMORPGs like EverQuest or World of Warcraft. Today, MUD can still be accessed for free. It’s definitely worth your attention.

notes.title: Steam Mystery Festival Wrap-up
notes.notes:
The Steam Mystery Festival came to a close recently and we loved watching streams of our game. We were actually in the Wild West over the festival and thought it’d be an idea to send out postcards to those who played the game live.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41825657/2ab860d4bc82d0bbce4c7aacf7869dbf818154c5.jpg[/img]

As well as participating, we managed to sneak off to investigate some truly wonderful mystery games also taking part in the festival. Here are some of our favourites:

[b]The Case of the Golden Idol[/b]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41825657/e1b9d5a789478a898a70ad523369cf4fe2029f5b.jpg[/img]
Something genuinely new and fresh, and with fantastic pixel art, The Case of the Golden Idol leaves the investigating firmly in your hands. Search for clues, motives and murder weapons and put them together in your notebook to solve each case. But get the wrong choices, and it’s curtains! We LOVED it.

[b]Grimfield Mystery[/b]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41825657/c62bf3812753a3c0fe5e5f8fe0a6421d98e9fc46.jpg[/img]
Cute and beautiful on the outside, deep and macabre on the inside! Grimfield Mystery features the small village of Grimfield, where the mystery is its middle name. The protagonist Lucas goes along with the wishes of his paranormal-loving parents to check out the local forest, and a new floating hand later, Lucas goes on his adventure!

[b]A Lonely Cabin Trip[/b]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41825657/f363ea22460836c0e672c24f619f2f91bedcb59a.jpg[/img]
When has a solo visit to an isolated island ever gone well? 
A Lonely Cabin Trip takes this premise and invites you on a psychological horror adventure with a genuine mystery to uncover. Have you visited before? It all looks familiar, but it shouldn’t, should it? There are different ways to solve problems with several endings too, plus it looks gorgeous!

[b]Wayward Strand[/b]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41825657/b38dd6ffffcaf5ba70393d03a229463072fc9469.jpg[/img]
This story-rich adventure left us wanting more. We have to learn about the lives of those living in an airborne hospital, explore the area and generally collect our stories for the school newspaper. Time continues for everyone, so if you don’t investigate one strand of a story, it’s gone til your next playthrough. A wonderful delight of a game.

We spoke to so many players, both old and new, who played Whispers in the West during the festival and saw a lovely bump in wishlists too! Thank you to everyone who tried out our game.

You can still play the demo and wishlist the game now!

Come over and join our Discord: [url=https://discord.gg/E9GvTQqvYu]https://discord.gg/E9GvTQqvYu[/url]

notes.title: Unravel our mystery this week!
notes.notes:
Today marks the start of the Steam Mystery Festival showcasing the best and brightest detective and mystery games available and coming soon. And you’re invited!

The ‘Mystery’ genre is not a new concept, with the very first graphical adventure game ever made being Mystery House in 1980, a ‘whodunit’ set in a creepy Victorian mansion. Fast forward 43 years and our very own mystery will be on its way soon!

When you’re unravelling a mystery, it’s handy to have a notebook of sorts to keep track of your ideas, possible suspects and motives, but sometimes you need a different way of thinking. You need a second pair of eyes. 

You need a team.

Whispers in the West, our multiplayer murder mystery, brings together all the vital parts of the mystery detective genre and adds co-op! When you’re stuck on a clue, a motive or a suspect you can have a discussion with your team and maybe broach a different theory. Sure it might be off-kilter, it may be a radical idea, but sharing with your friends is what gaming is about! You may all align your thoughts and crack the case, or you may discuss at length and still disagree on the who, the what and the why. But in the end, you’ll have to come together to decide who you think is the culprit.

Whispers in the West can be played with up to 4 players, each member of the team picking a different character to play. Will you be the tough Sheriff and use your badge to calm down a suspect? Or maybe the lawless cowboy, shooting from the hip with his gun, ready to scare the truth out of people? Each character has their own unique skill to help, and hinder the case.

We’d love for you to try out Whispers in the West and stream it with your friends. The game can also be played as a 1 player game. 

The demo features the first case and is fully available to play right now. 

Download here: [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/1868070/Whispers_in_the_West__Multiplayer_Murder_Mystery/]https://store.steampowered.com/app/1868070/Whispers_in_the_West__Multiplayer_Murder_Mystery/
[/url]

notes.title: Major update: Soundtracks, In-game Voice Chat and more
notes.notes:
Thank you for your support of Whispers in the West. Since we released the demo during Steam Next Fest, more than 1500 players have tried it, and 1200 players have wishlisted the game on Steam so far.

We’re delighted by the positive feedback we received from many of you, and we’ve not sat back since the launch of the demo. After nearly two months of hard work, we’re delighted to  introduce a few exciting new features:

[b]Soundtracks[/b]
This is music to our ears!! We’ve now included two beautifully composed tracks “Confronting the Man in Black” and “We Don’t Need Railroads” from Harvey Carmen(@composercarman ) in the game. Besides being a talented musician, Harvey has also been a long-time patron of Whispers in the West.

[b]In-game Voice Chat[/b]
We’ve made it easier for you to communicate with your friends by incorporating voice chat in the game. Of course, you can still use your favourite voice chat software like Discord if you prefer. 

[b]Improved Message Pinning feature[/b]
Now you can pin messages directly in the dialogues, and pinned messages will be broadcast to your party, making it easier to take notes and community with your teammates.

[b]Enhanced Case Report UI[/b]
We have reworked the Case Report UI.

[b]Game Flow Highlighting[/b]
We have made it simpler and easier to follow the flow of the game. 

[b]Unity Analytics[/b]
To help us identify and analyse any technical issues, we introduced Unity Analytics. This means we can fix bugs more quickly, leaving you and your team to solve the case with no interruptions. You can opt in/out of this feature in the game.

Adjusted scaling on certain aspects of the outro cinematic for the ghost script.

[b]Networking[/b]
Added an error popup when you are disconnected from the Photon Network. 
When you are disconnected from the Photon Network, you will be automatically returned to the main menu where the game will try to reconnect automatically.

[b]Fixes[/b]
Portrait no longer disappears in the ghost script.
Various UI positioning fixes.
As a result of fixing disconnections from the photon network, players should no longer run into an issue where their character vanishes and becomes zoomed in.
